text: Rollback preservation: a rollback reported as succeeded leaves the prior image running and tagged.
A failure before the restart stage leaves Docker untouched (tag and container on prior).
A terminal operation keeps its journal record only when it failed past the write-ahead barrier and no inline rollback passed its gate and verify (ADR-0062 slice 1).
A terminal operation whose inline rollback passed its gate and verify has retired its journal record.
A succeeded terminal operation has retired its journal record.
A failed rollback is always reported as rollback_failed.
Rollback is attempted only after a post-restart failure, when enabled, with a valid prior digest.

Write-ahead barrier: while an operation is in flight, the tag is on the target only if the journal durably says so. (A record a converge start retired after adopting the verified target is no longer in flight.)
Once a successful restart is journaled with the target running, the record names it as its target image id.

text: The journal never names an image that is not the target as the target image id (ADR-0061 F1).

text: The journal phase never moves backwards.
In the apply flow, only the rollback restart stage moves the tag off the target. (A converge start's tag moves are R2/R3.)
In the apply flow, the running image changes only inside a restart stage. (A converge start's restarts are R1/R4.)
Agent restart after a crash only marks the operation interrupted; it does not touch Docker or the journal.
Recovery: once a rollback is armed it resolves (succeeds or is reported failed) within 4 stages.
Recovery is achievable: with a healthy prior image an armed rollback can succeed.
Every operation stops (terminal or crashed) within 12 stages.
Reconcile never answers no-op while the tag is ahead of the running container.
